papers.title: Next-generation pharmacological strategies for Parkinson's disease: a systematic literature review of symptom management and disease modification.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: Parkinson disease is an ongoing neurodegenerative disorder, and both motor and non-motor symptoms are involved with the existing therapies having minimal effects on the disease but only symptom alleviation. The goal of this systematic literature review was to generalize up-to-date evidence on the next-generation pharmacological strategies to manage the symptoms and the disease in a patient with Parkinson disease. The review was based on PRISMA 2020 and included the analysis of peer-reviewed studies of human research published in 2015-2026 and retrieved in the key databases, such as PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library. This included 30 eligible studies consisting of randomized studies, observational studies, and early clinical trials. The results show that, although dopaminergic treatment continues to play a central role in managing motor symptoms, new methods such as gene therapy, gene editing, stem cell-based regeneration, nanomedicine delivery systems, repurposed drugs, artificial intelligence-based precision medicine approaches have a good neuroprotective and disease-modifying potential. Nonetheless, the majority of new interventions are still in preclinical or first line clinical phase, with a defined subset of emerging gene-, cell-, and nanotechnology-based approaches evaluated only in animal or in-vitro models rather than in PD patients and associated with small sample size, invasive delivery, limited follow-up and lack of long-term safety information. In general, the review concludes by stating that there has been significant advancement in diversification of therapeutic targets and mechanisms, but rigorous large-scale biomarker-directed clinical trials are needed to translate these advances to effective and sustainable treatment of the Parkinson disease.

papers.title: Consistency of Serial Cerebrospinal Fluid α-Synuclein Seed Amplification Assay Results in the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Studies reporting α-synuclein seed amplification assay (aSyn-SAA) results are often cross-sectional. OBJECTIVES: In this study, we investigated the intraindividual consistency of aSyn-SAA results (Amprion) over time from participants in the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI). METHODS: A total of 1238 participants had >1 cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) aSyn-SAA result for analysis (Parkinson's disease [PD] = 633, prodromal = 563, healthy control [HC] = 42), collected over a median (minimum, maximum) of 2.0 (0.4, 11.4) years. Emphasis was placed on evaluating consistency in aSyn-SAA-PD participants, aSyn-SAA + HC participants, and conversion rates from aSyn-SAA negative to positive results prodromal participants. RESULTS: Of aSyn-SAA + PD participants, 96% (474/493, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 94%-98%) remained positive in subsequent samples, and 92% (116/126, 95% CI: 86%-96%) of aSyn-SAA-PD participants remained negative. Ninety-nine percent (303/307, 95% CI: 97%-99%) of aSyn-SAA + prodromal participants remained positive, and 95% (234/247, 95% CI: 91%-97%) of aSyn-SAA-prodromal participants remained negative. Eighty-nine percent (16/18, 95% CI: 67%-97%) of aSyn-SAA + HC participants remained positive, and 87% (20/23, 95% CI: 68%-95%) of aSyn-SAA-HC participants remained negative. CONCLUSIONS: aSyn-SAA testing is highly consistent over time, even in less expected scenarios. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.title: Evaluation of peripheral and intranigral AAV-mediated Irisin delivery in a chronic AAV-A53T α-Synuclein overexpression mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and pathological aggregation of α-Synuclein (α-Syn). Although Irisin has shown neuroprotective effects in acute MPTP-induced and α-Syn preformed fibrils (PFFs) propagation models, its therapeutic effects in a chronic α-Syn overexpression model remain incompletely defined. METHODS: In the present study, we evaluated the effects of AAV8-Irisin delivered either peripherally via tail vein injection or centrally via direct intranigral co-administration in the AAV9-A53T mouse model. RESULTS: Under the tested doses, routes, and intervention schedule, neither peripheral nor intranigral AAV8-Irisin delivery produced statistically significant improvements in behavioral performance, dopaminergic neuron survival, α-Synuclein pathology, glial activation, or AQP4 polarization; however, numerical trends were observed in select measures, including motor coordination and TH-positive neuron counts. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that, under the current experimental conditions, a clear neuroprotective benefit of Irisin was not readily detectable in this model. Whether modest effects might emerge under different exposure levels, intervention windows, or adequately powered designs remains unknown.

papers.title: Normative Modeling of Amygdala Subfields and Disease-Specific Vulnerabilities Across Neurological Disorders.
papers.abstract: As an integrative center of the limbic system, the amygdala and its subfields participate in diverse neural functions and demonstrate heterogeneous structural changes in various neurological disorders. In this study, three-dimensional T1-weighted MRI data from 22,258 healthy participants were analyzed using normative modeling to establish normative references for the volumes of the amygdala and its subfields. These models elucidated the developmental and aging curves of the amygdala and identified distinct ages at peak volume across subfields, ranging from 24.6 to 43.7 years. Based on these references, individual centile scores were calculated for 4132 patients with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, cerebral small vessel disease, multiple sclerosis, and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder. These centile scores not only captured disease-specific deviation patterns of the amygdala subfields but also demonstrated utility in disease classification. Moreover, the centile scores correlated with clinical measures of cognitive function, emotional state, and motor performance across disorders. These findings suggest that normative references of the amygdala subfields provide insights into cross-disease alteration patterns and offer potential neuroimaging biomarkers to aid differential diagnosis and clinical assessment.

papers.title: Bacteria-Derived 1-Allylpiperazine Alleviates Symptoms of Parkinson's Disease Model by Promoting Autophagy.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with no available disease-modifying therapies. Given their diverse health-promoting properties, probiotics have emerged as a potential neuroprotective strategy. Through screening in transgenic Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) models of α-synuclein (α-syn)-induced PD, we identified the Escherichia coli (E. coli) strain E8 as a candidate that effectively suppressed dendritic degeneration and motor deficits. These neuroprotective improvements were attributed to the reduction of α-syn aggregation, which was mechanistically associated with E8's ability to promote autophagy. Metabolomic profiling further pinpointed 1-allylpiperazine (1-ALPP) as a bioactive metabolite responsible for rescuing PD-related impairments, which was sufficient to recapitulate the autophagy activation induced by E8. Subsequent mechanistic studies revealed that 1-ALPP activated autophagy through the AMPK/mTOR/HLH-30 pathway. Notably, 1-ALPP effectively inhibited α-syn fibrillogenesis and cytotoxicity in a dose-dependent manner, potentially via the inhibition of α-syn liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). Molecular simulations demonstrated that 1-ALPP binds to α-syn, thereby preventing the critical conformational changes required for fibril formation. Strikingly, the protective effects of E8 against PD phenotypes were intergenerationally inherited, persisting for two generations in an hpl-2-dependent manner.

papers.title: Therapeutic potential of neural stem cell-derived exosomes and PRP in Parkinson's disease: A novel regenerative approach.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurological ailment characterized by oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and the progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra. The current treatments lack disease-modifying capabilities. The current study investigated the neuroprotective and regenerative efficacy of a combination of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NMSC-EXO) and PRP in a rotenone-induced rat model of PD. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Thirty male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to three equal groups (n = 10/group). Group I (negative Control): received subcutaneous (s.c) sunflower oil for 35 days followed by intravenous (i.v.) saline for 30 days. Group II (Rotenone model): administered 2 mg/kg/day rotenone s.c. for 35 days followed by i.v. saline for 30 days; Group III Rotenone + combination (Exosomes + PRP): received 2 mg/kg/day rotenone s.c. for 35 days, followed by biweekly i.v. injection of 109 RESULTS: The co-administration of NMSC-EXO and PRP significantly attenuated rotenone-induced motor deficits, thereby restoring locomotor activity, balance, and exploratory behavior. Dual therapy preserved dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, downregulated the apoptotic marker caspase-1, and significantly decreased lipid peroxidation (MDA) while restoring reduced glutathione (GSH) levels. Furthermore, treatment led to significant upregulation of tyrosine hydroxylase and integrin expression relative to the rotenone model group. CONCLUSION: Combined NMSC-EXO and PRP therapy exerted strong neuroprotective, antioxidant, and anti-apoptotic effects against rotenone-induced neurotoxicity. This synergetic approach represents a novel, cell-free regenerative strategy for Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: Multiplexed impedimetric zinc oxide nanorods-modified aptasensor on carbon ink-inscribed paper electrodes for the specific and sensitive co-detection of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), represent a growing health burden, while early diagnosis remains challenging because established diagnostic approaches, including cerebrospinal fluid analysis and neuroimaging, are invasive, expensive, and unsuitable for decentralized point-of-care testing. Recent progress in electrochemical and paper-based biosensors has enabled low-cost, portable, and multiplexed biomarker analysis. However, their clinical translation remains limited by low biomarker concentrations, matrix interference, nonspecific adsorption, sensor-to-sensor variability, storage stability, and the need for validation using clinical samples. Herein, a paper-based multiplex electrochemical aptasensor was developed for simultaneous impedimetric detection of amyloid beta-42 (Aβ-42) and alpha synuclein-60 (αS-60), biomarkers associated with AD and PD, respectively. The device comprised screen-printed carbon and silver electrodes on a cellulose substrate, two independently functionalized working electrodes, zinc oxide nanorods (ZnO-NRs) as electroactive signal-amplification layers, and target-specific DNA aptamers as biorecognition elements. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy was used for label-free measurement of target-induced changes in charge-transfer resistance. The sensor exhibited a linear response from 0.1 ng/mL to 10 µg/mL for both biomarkers, with limits of detection of 4.41 ng/mL for Aβ-42 and 2.62 ng/mL for αS-60. The platform further detected both analytes in artificial cerebrospinal fluid and artificial saliva, demonstrating that the paper-based sensing interface remains responsive in physiologically mimicked matrices. Overall, this study provides a low-cost, disposable, label-free, and multiplexed proof-of-concept platform for simultaneous AD- and PD-associated biomarker detection. papers.title: Spontaneous eye behavior is an objective marker of parkinsonian severity.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.abstract: Eye behavior disruption is reported in Parkinson's disease (PD), but its correlation with disease severity has not been well examined. Here, in a nonhuman primate model of PD, we show that spontaneous eye behavior is impaired in parkinsonism and correlates with clinical rating scores and subthalamic beta oscillatory activity. These findings suggest that spontaneous eye behavior could serve as an objective, non-invasive biomarker of parkinsonian severity.

papers.title: A New Frontier in CWD Detection: Antemortem Plasma Biomarkers and Behavioral Profiling in Transgenic Mouse Models.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.abstract: Chronic Wasting Disease (CWD) is a fatal transmissible spongiform encephalopathy (TSE) that is confined to cervids (deer, moose, elk, and reindeer) but shares key properties with human neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's disease and frontal-temporal dementia. CWD and other TSEs are caused by the misfolded prion protein (PrP). Although the identification of diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers at all stages of disease progression is becoming exceedingly critical as CWD continues to increase in prevalence, accurate antemortem testing techniques are extremely limited. This study made use of cervidized transgenic mice (mice carrying the cervid PrP) that recapitulate CWD in various disease stages and investigated the utility of neurological biomarkers and neurobehavioral manifestations for CWD detection. Neurofilament light chain (NFL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and total Tau (t-Tau) were assessed under the hypothesis that combined biomarker signatures might more reliably reflect CWD-related neurodegeneration and disease progression. Analyses at 90, 132, 174, and 230 days post-CWD inoculation show distinct biomarker elevation, with all three biomarkers significantly elevated in the CWD animals by 132 days post-inoculation. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that these three plasma biomarkers are useful not only for detecting CWD, but also for identifying it at early antemortem stages of disease. Novel phenotypes were also revealed by comprehensive phenotypic profiling, including rigid tail elevation, increased grip strength, and impaired coordination, to lend further support to plasma biomarker data indicating neurologic impairment associated with brain pathology. Ultimately, the goal is to improve antemortem, non-invasive CWD detection methods to enable earlier detection and assist with disease management.

papers.title: PPARγ Signaling in the Central Nervous System: A Review of the Implications in Synaptic Plasticity, Neuroinflammatory and Neoplastic Processes.
papers.abstract: Peroxisome proliferator activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) is a ligand activated nuclear receptor traditionally associated with lipid and glucose metabolism. Emerging evidence, however, identifies PPARγ as a central immunometabolic regulator in the central nervous system (CNS), coordinating mitochondrial function, neuroinflammation, synaptic plasticity, and neurovascular integrity. Beyond its classical metabolic actions, PPARγ regulates microglial activation, astrocytic inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial biogenesis, thereby influencing neuronal resilience and circuit stability. This narrative review synthesizes knowledge of PPARγ structure, activation, CNS distribution, endogenous ligands, and synthetic agonists, including thiazolidinediones and selective modulators. We highlight how PPARγ controls transcriptional programs related to energy homeostasis, inflammatory signaling, including NF κB dependent pathways, and blood brain barrier function. Attention is devoted to synaptic remodeling and plasticity, positioning PPARγ as a molecular bridge between metabolic state and neuronal adaptability. We propose that PPARγ signaling dysregulation represents a convergent mechanism in neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and adrenoleukodystrophy; psychiatric conditions, such as depression and anxiety; and neurooncological processes. Integrating evidence across these conditions supports PPARγ as a master regulator of neuroimmune metabolic coupling in the brain. Finally, we discuss translational challenges and opportunities, including brain penetrant, functionally selective ligands, clarification of cell type specific signaling, and expansion of rigorous clinical trials. papers.title: Effects of globus pallidus internus deep brain stimulation on freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease: a prospective short-term single-arm study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Freezing of gait (FoG) is a debilitating symptom in Parkinson's disease (PD), often resistant to medication. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) has emerged as an effective treatment for advanced PD, while its effect on FoG remains inconsistent. Specifically, the effect of globus pallidus internus deep brain stimulation (GPi-DBS) against FoG is inconclusive, and relevant studies are scarce. OBJECTIVE: To describe the post-operative effect of GPi-DBS on FoG and identify pre-operative predictors of improvement. METHODS: Forty-six PD patients undergoing GPi-DBS were assessed pre-operatively and at short-term follow-up (a median of 11 months) using the Gait and Falls Questionnaire (GFQ) and a comprehensive Timed Up and Go (TUG) test that quantified five FoG-related TUG indices. The primary outcome was the within-individual change in TUG total time, computed as the pre-operative med-off value minus the DBS-on med-off value. The secondary outcomes were changes of pre-operative med-off vs. med-on (the acute levodopa response) and pre-operative med-off vs. DBS-off med-off (a within-subject negative control for disease progression). Pre-operative predictors of FoG were assessed to predict the within-individual change in the TUG indices by performing forward stepwise Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) regression analysis. RESULTS: At short-term follow-up, FoG measures (the TUG-derived indices and the self-reported GFQ) improved after GPi-DBS. TUG total time decreased by a median of 5.0 s (95% CI 1.5-14.5; FDR = 0.003), and the longest FoG duration by 1.0 s (95% CI 0-3.5; FDR = 0.030); the other three TUG indices improved in the same direction but did not survive correction (FDR 0.064-0.080). papers.title: Preoperative neuropsychological prognostic factors for deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Preoperative neuropsychological evaluation is standard in deep brain stimulation (DBS) candidacy assessment for Parkinson's disease (PD), but batteries vary substantially across centers and may require 6-8 h across multiple visits. OBJECTIVES: To synthesize evidence on preoperative neuropsychological prognostic factors for cognitive, functional, behavioral, speech, and quality-of-life outcomes following DBS and develop an evidence-informed assessment framework. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through May 19, 2026. Eligible studies reported an identifiable preoperative neuropsychological measure associated with DBS candidacy or selection or with a postoperative outcome assessed at least 6 months after surgery. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using QUIPS and PROBAST. Evidence certainty was evaluated using GRADE. RESULTS: Thirty-four studies comprising 3783 DBS patients were included. Among 311 extracted results, 238 involved an identifiable prognostic predictor, of which 117 (49.2%) reported adjusted multivariable estimates. Global cognition, executive function, and memory were evaluated as prognostic predictors in 21, 17, and 8 studies, respectively, with generally supportive directions when determinable. MDRS/DRS was most extensively studied but frequently directionally indeterminate, whereas MoCA, semantic/category fluency, and WCST each showed supportive directions in at least two studies. No instrument demonstrated comparative prognostic superiority. CONCLUSIONS: Global cognition, executive function, and memory showed generally supportive but low-certainty prognostic associations. Based on these findings and consensus recommendations, we propose a standardized framework incorporating a clinical interview and streamlined testing battery requiring approximately 2 h to improve efficiency, consistency, and comparability across centers.

papers.title: Preoperative Functional Imaging Predicts Deep Brain Stimulation Outcome in Craniocervical Dystonia.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is an established treatment for craniocervical dystonia (CCD), yet postoperative benefit varies widely and cannot be estimated before surgery. Resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) has shown prognostic value across DBS indications. The objective of this study was to develop and externally validate preoperative rs-fMRI models estimating DBS response in CCD. METHODS: Forty-two patients from two independent centers underwent preoperative 3 T rs-fMRI (discovery, n = 26; validation, n = 16). Using 12 literature-informed, symptom-relevant regions of interest, we quantified the amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation as a measure of intrinsic regional neural activity. We applied regularized modeling to classify super-responders, distinguish responders from non-responders, and estimate improvement in Burke-Fahn-Marsden Dystonia Rating Scale motor subscore. RESULTS: When applied to the validation cohort, the imaging models achieved a three-category classification accuracy of 75.0% (50.5%-89.8%) using a sequential two-step procedure (Pperm CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative rs-fMRI captures clinically relevant variation in baseline brain state in CCD, with predictive performance supported in an external validation. These findings provide preliminary support for rs-fMRI as a potential source of information to aid patient counseling and clinical decision-making, pending prospective validation. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

papers.title: Effects of dual-task training on health-related quality of life and cognitive function in people with Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Dual-task training is proposed as a rehabilitative strategy to mitigate motor and cognitive impairments in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD). This systematic review and meta-analysis sought to consolidate existing information regarding the impact of dual-task therapies on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and cognitive performance in middle-aged and older persons diagnosed with PD. METHODS: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published to May 2026 was performed utilizing PubMed, EBSCOhost, Scopus, and Web of Science. The chosen studies adhered to the PICOS framework. The Methodological quality and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and GRADE framework, respectively. The review protocol is recorded in PROSPERO under the number CRD420251159680. RESULTS: Out of 3,037 identified records, 10 RCTs met the eligibility criteria and were included in the systematic review, of which 9 contributed data to the meta-analysis. The meta-analysis showed a statistically significant but modest effect on HRQoL measured with the Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire-39 (SMD = 0.35; 95% CI: 0.03-0.67; p = CONCLUSION: Dual-task interventions may produce a modest improvement in HRQoL in people with Parkinson's disease, whereas the current evidence does not demonstrate significant benefits for the cognitive outcomes assessed. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of studies, methodological limitations, and clinical heterogeneity across interventions. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251159680, identifier CRD420251159680.

papers.title: Aging-driven Mechanisms Underlying Parkinson's Disease Pathogenesis: Molecular, Cellular, and Systemic Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for Parkinson's Disease (PD) and is linked to various biological processes at the molecular, cellular, and systemic levels. At the molecular level, aging-related oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, genetic factors, and impaired proteostasis contribute to dopaminergic neuronal death. Cellular alterations include persistent glial cell activation, autophagylysosomal dysfunction, and impaired cellular repair mechanisms. At the systemic level, aging is associated with metabolic imbalance, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and immune system dysfunction, which may contribute to PD pathogenesis through the gut-brain axis. Antioxidant therapy, stem cell therapy, anti-aging agents, and modulation of gut-brain communication have shown promise in the management of PD. Lifestyle modifications, including dietary changes and regular exercise, may exert anti-aging effects that could help delay or prevent the onset of PD. Emerging anti-aging interventions, including N-acetylcysteine and plant-derived compounds that support mitochondrial function, have also demonstrated therapeutic potential for PD.

papers.title: Freezing of Gait: A Therapeutic Perspective.
papers.abstract: Despite improved definition of the problem and better understanding of its phenomenology, freezing of gait (FoG) remains a therapeutic enigma for clinicians and neuroscientists alike. Patients with Parkinson disease (PD) or other neurological disorders experiencing FoG are similarly frustrated, despite the benefits that levodopa and other medications provide for control of PD's primary motor features. For those burdened by episodes of FoG, current therapeutic options are quite limited. Some patients achieve improvements from pharmacotherapy-for example, by adjunctive use of an oral dopaminergic agonist or by subcutaneous infusion of apomorphine. If needed, deep brain stimulation sometimes offers symptomatic improvements. Certain interventions devised by physical therapists (or discovered by patients themselves) can improve FoG. However, successful pharmacotherapy for FoG has lagged behind, though the future holds some promising leads for therapies acting on dopaminergic, adenosinergic, noradrenergic, glutamatergic, and cholinergic circuitry.

papers.title: State of the "Art" in Freezing of Gait: Drawing on Perspectives of Individuals With Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Freezing of gait (FoG) in Parkinson's disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a multidimensional phenomenon encompassing motor, cognitive, and emotional domains. The impact of FoG is enormous, but can be difficult to articulate. Traditional clinical assessments typically fail to capture its subjective and affective impact. This qualitative study explored drawings from individuals with PD to better understand the lived experience of FoG. Specifically, we collected artworks created by individuals who experience FoG. We studied the personal perceptions and emotions associated with FoG drawings in two ways: by asking participants to narratively explain their artwork and a qualitative curation by an international panel of experts of neurology, neuroscience, neurorehabilitation, neuroaesthetics, art, and empirical aesthetics. Five overarching themes emerged: (1) "Captured feet," depicting sensations of being glued, tethered, or rooted to the ground; (2) "Chaos," reflecting disrupted motor control during environmental or cognitive overload; (3) "Emotional explosion," expressing fear, anger, helplessness, and loss of control; (4) "Freezing and falls," highlighting instability and existential threat; and (5) "Released from freeze," portraying therapeutic relief, restored movement, and joy. These visual narratives reveal that FoG is more than just a motor block. Rather, it is an embodied experience of immobilization, emotional escalation, and vulnerability, contrasted by profound relief when mobility returns. Artistic expression offers unique insights beyond structured assessments, fostering empathetic clinician-patient communication, and supporting a more holistic, person-centered approach to PD care.

papers.title: The Impact of Neuropalliative Care on Caregivers of Individuals with Motor Neuron Disorders or Atypical Parkinsonism.
papers.journal: Journal of hospice and palliative nursing : JHPN : the official journal of the Hospice and Palliative Nurses Association
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders, including motor neuron disease (MND) and atypical parkinsonism (AP), progress rapidly and place substantial physical, emotional, and financial strain on family caregivers who often provide complex care with limited support. Neuropalliative care (NPC) offers interdisciplinary, noncurative services aimed at improving quality of life (QoL), yet it is underutilized and often misunderstood. Employing Ferrans and Powers QoL Model, this study used an exploratory descriptive qualitative design to examine the experiences of 10 family caregivers of individuals with MND and AP receiving NPC at a specialized clinic. Thematically analyzed semi-structured interviews produced 4 themes that were identified: (1) caregiver QoL, (2) caregiver burden, (3) support, and (4) system barriers. Caregivers described significant emotional and physical strain, loss of personal time, and financial pressures. Clinic services such as anticipatory guidance, interdisciplinary support, and resource navigation were valued; however, many caregivers were unaware they were receiving NPC. Caregivers of individuals with MND reported broader access to resources than those supporting individuals with AP, who experienced more systemic barriers. Findings emphasize the need for earlier NPC integration; increasing awareness of services provided, improving caregiver education, and ensuring equitable access. These steps are necessary for enhancing caregiver well-being and optimizing care outcomes in this population.
